figs.title: Cauchy, first Piola and second Piola stress
figs.caption: The same force df on a material face can be measured three ways. Cauchy stress uses the current area n da, the first Piola stress uses the reference area N dA, and the second Piola stress also pulls the force back by F⁻¹, which makes it symmetric and blind to rigid rotations.

figs.title: Tube inflation: held ends versus closed ends
figs.caption: With its length held, a neo-Hookean tube needs steadily more pressure, approaching μT/R. With closed free ends the tube also lengthens, the pressure peaks near λ_θ ≈ 1.58, and a bulge then grows at falling pressure.

figs.title: Material derivative: local plus convective
figs.caption: Following one particle, its velocity change splits into the local change of the field at a fixed point and the convective change from moving to a point where the field is faster. Their sum per unit time is Dv/Dt.
